audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagreed with the packet chart and with their own whys — most badly level 6, where the chart handed the row to Karma while whys[4] calls Explosive Cask into Body Slam a game-ender, and 2+ items, given to Gragas while whys[6] says Karma reclaims range.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Skill, Skill, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Karma and the gragas__karma mirror was already set to exactly that. whys[2] and whys[3] both describe even trades, which is Skill, not Gragas.
audit.corrected: Rows 2,3 -> Skill; row 4 -> Gragas; row 6 -> Karma, proposed as matched full/content pairs in one atomic group (rows 0,1,5 already agreed).

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items stage was described as generic drift to utility with no reason the stage belongs to anyone.
audit.why: Body Slam is 600 range on 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s and is his only gap-closer; Karma's Inner Flame is 950. Once she has haste items and his combo is on cooldown she simply out-distances him, which is why the packet gives her the row.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why and whys[6] now name the 600 range and Body Slam's 14s rank-1 cooldown as the reason the stage flips back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Explosive Cask was described as knocking you 'toward him', which is not what it does; 'Soulflare' was used as the name of the Mantra-empowered Q; and the Drunken Rage auto-reset tell was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text says Explosive Cask knocks enemies back from the blast — so the shove is away from the cask's impact point, which is why he lands it on the far side of you to push you into his hands. Drunken Rage is a 1-second sample that empowers his NEXT basic attack, so the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step out. Riot names no Soulflare.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten to state the knock-back-from-impact mechanic; the W wind-up written into the do's; Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q in the fields edited.
sources: kit: Gragas R 'knocking back enemies caught in the blast radius'

edits.before: Explosive Cask (R) knocks you toward him into a guaranteed Body Slam follow-up — a true game-ender his short range otherwise lacks.
edits.after: Explosive Cask knocks back from its impact point, so he lands it behind you to shove you into a Body Slam — the finisher his 600 range lacks.

edits.before: His combo on cooldown lets you reclaim range — RQ zone-poke, RE shields, and a W root on his dash kite a brawler you out-distance.
edits.after: With Body Slam down 14s at rank 1 you reclaim range — Mantra-Q zones, Mantra-E shields and a root on his dash kite a 600-range brawler.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: You out-distance a 600-range brawler now — zone with Mantra-Q, shield the Cask, and root him after the dash.

edits.before: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Engage and escape in one button, down 14s at rank 1 — his W wind-up is the tell, so step back on that, not the cast.

edits.before: Open with RQ Soulflare on him before he has Body Slam (E) — it's your one window where he can't dash onto you to answer the delayed-zone poke.
edits.after: Open with Mantra-Q on him before he has Body Slam (E) — it is your one window where he cannot dash onto you to answer the delayed-zone poke.

edits.before: Land the Lvl 1 RQ Soulflare before Body Slam exists, then chip him with Inner Flame (Q) on his last-hits
edits.after: Land the level 1 Mantra-Q before Body Slam exists, then chip with Inner Flame from 950 on his last-hits

notes: The gragas__karma mirror asserts you can 'break line of sight to cancel the root' on Focused Resolve. Riot's text only says the tether breaks if it is not maintained, and the karma__gnar mirror auditor removed the same line-of-sight claim as unsupported. I did not repeat it here — the 675 distance break is what the kit actually supports. Recorded in unverified so the two mirrors can be reconciled by whoever owns gragas.
